title: Cell-Free Methylation Fragmentomics for Stage I–II Pancreatic Cancer Triage in High-Risk Cyst Surveillance
authors_line: Victor K. Sato, PhD¹; Miriam Alverez, MD¹
affiliations_line: ¹Synthetic Translational Oncology Laboratory (Synthetic Demonstration Study)
headline_takeaway: Locked plasma cfDNA fragmentomic score achieved 87.3% sensitivity (96/110) and 92.5% specificity (185/200) in blinded external validation (N = 310).

items.title: 01  Translational Rationale
paragraphs: CA19-9 lacks sensitivity for early-stage pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and Lewis-antigen-negative patients.
bullets: Assay: Targeted bisulfite-free methylation + 5'-end motif fragmentomics from 4 mL peripheral plasma.
Blinded External Validation: N = 310 prospective biobank samples (110 Stage I–II PDAC; 200 mucinous/serous cysts & healthy controls).

items.title: 02  Controls & Limitations
bullets: Pre-analytical hemolysis and acute pancreatitis spikes can elevate background cfDNA yield.
Prospective asymptomatic screening positive-predictive-value requires longitudinal cohort follow-up.

items.title: 03  Fragmentomic Risk Score Distribution Across Stages
items.caption: Figure 1. Distribution of locked plasma fragmentomic scores across benign controls and Stage I–II PDAC (synthetic sample distributions).

items.title: 04  Blinded Validation Contingency Matrix
items.caption: Figure 2. Blinded validation matrix (N = 310): Sensitivity 87.3% (96/110), Specificity 92.5% (185/200).

items.title: 05  Conclusions
paragraphs: Combined cfDNA methylation and end-motif profiling distinguishes early-stage resectable PDAC from benign pancreatic cysts with >92% specificity.
